title: Fractal geometry misses complexity by excluding interactions between elements

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fractal geometry misses complexity by excluding interactions between elements

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Traditional fractal geometry does not consider interactions between elements, which is why all patterns it produces are purely nested; allowing replacements to depend on neighbors on a grid readily yields complicated, non-nested patterns.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: in traditional fractal geometry the idea of interaction between elements is not considered—so that all patterns that are produced have a purely nested form.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Substitution Systems and Fractals” (from p. 187), p. 190. Scope: fractal geometry and two-dimensional neighbor-dependent substitution systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mathematical contrast between context-free and context-sensitive replacement can be tested and partly proved. The causal historical assertion about an entire field and all its patterns is too broad for existing literature coverage to resolve completely.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Survey formal fractal constructions for context dependence, prove nesting for context-free replacements, and computationally compare them with matched neighbor-dependent systems using hierarchy and complexity measures. Counterexamples from traditional fractal geometry with interacting elements would refute the historical taxonomy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Misses complexity is evaluative.

Neighbor dependence is sufficient for some non-nested outputs but not necessary for all notions of complexity.

Traditional fractal geometry is historically broad and not a formal class.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The computational half is direct: neighbor-dependent grid substitutions can be run, and non-nested outputs confirm that allowing interactions produces patterns outside pure nesting. The claim that traditional fractal geometry misses complexity because it excludes interactions is a characterization of a field, and a simulation does not decide how that field is defined. Existing computation therefore settles the constructive half only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate two-dimensional substitution rules in which the replacement depends on neighboring cells, and test whether the result is a purely nested self-similar pattern. A persistent non-nested pattern confirms the computational half; the historical claim that traditional fractal geometry excludes interactions is a separate judgment about the literature.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
What 'traditional fractal geometry' considers is a historical classification and can be disputed by pointing at exceptions in the literature.

A neighbor-dependent rule can still be nested, so one nested example does not refute 'readily yields' non-nested patterns.
